blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: In eXplainable AI, counterfactual explanations have gained significant traction by offering users direct, intuitive, and actionable insights into model decisions. We introduce CounterFlow, a novel framework based on Conditional Flow Matching that generates visual counterfactual explanations by directly steering a source image toward a user-specified target class. By leveraging target-conditioned vector fields, CounterFlow identifies highly realistic semantic modifications while requiring substantially lower computational overhead than traditional GAN- or diffusion-based architectures. Empirical evaluations on standard benchmarks demonstrate that CounterFlow achieves state-of-the-art performance in both visual realism and target class switching. By working directly in the raw pixel space, CounterFlow offers a more practical solution for real-world deployment.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Context. On the one hand, in generative modeling, diffusion models currently dominate the landscape for high-quality image, video, and audio synthesis ( Rombach et al., 2022 ; Ho et al., 2022 ; Liu et al., 2023a ) .
However, they are also well-known for their slow training times and their stochastic sampling paths.
To address these limitations, Lipman et al. (2023) ; Albergo and Vanden-Eijnden (2023) ; Liu et al. (2023b) introduced Conditional Flow Matching (CFM).
CFM is a generative modeling framework based on Continuous Normalizing Flows (CNFs) that uses standard regression objectives for training.
Moreover, instead of relying on diffusion processes, CFM generates examples by integrating the CNF’s ODE along deterministic trajectories.
On the other hand, the generative models’ ability to generate complex data distributions and thus to produce realistic examples is particularly appealing for eXplainable Artificial Intelligence ( Dwivedi et al., 2023 , XAI,) , where one aims to produce counterfactual explanations ( Wachter et al., 2017 ) , i.e. , examples (i) close to a given input, (ii) plausible, and (iii) that change the model’s prediction.
Unlike adversarial examples that rely on imperceptible noise to fool the classifier, counterfactual examples expose meaningful changes, helping users to trust the model while enabling developers to debug it.
Our work leverages CFM to create counterfactual explanations: rather than generating images from random noise, our approach transports an input sample toward a counterfactual conditioned on a user-defined target class, while jointly optimizing for plausibility and proximity; see Figure 1 .

blocks.en:
Related Work. Prior work on image counterfactual explanations falls into two categories: instance-based and generative approaches.
Instance-based methods ( Goyal et al., 2019 ; Keane and Smyth, 2020 , see e.g. ,) select examples from the training set using similarity metrics to modify the input sample 𝐱 \mathbf{x} .
However, they require access to the training set at inference and cannot tailor a minimal, plausible edit to a specific example 𝐱 \mathbf{x} .
We focus instead on generative approaches, a more recent line of work ( Khorram and Fuxin, 2022 ; Jeanneret et al., 2024 ; Weng et al., 2024 ; Augustin et al., 2022 ; Cao et al., 2025 ) that produces more plausible examples, which we group by generative backbone: GANs, diffusion models, or CFM. • GAN. C3LT ( Khorram and Fuxin, 2022 ) encodes the input (with a VAE encoder) into a latent space, in which it learns two cycle-consistent transformations per pair of classes ( y , y ′ ) (y,y^{\prime}) before decoding with the generator of a GAN.
It thus requires one model set per pair, impractical for many classes, and its fidelity is bounded by the VAE’s reconstruction quality. • Diffusion. DiME ( Jeanneret et al., 2024 ) generates a counterfactual by corrupting the input and denoising it through the backward diffusion process (an inner loop of several steps); at each outer step, the classifier gradient computed on this denoised estimate refines the corrupted instance, and the process repeats until it converges to a valid counterfactual.
FastDiME ( Weng et al., 2024 ) instead computes this gradient directly from the model’s one-step denoised estimate, bypassing the inner loop entirely.
ACE ( Jeanneret et al., 2023 ) takes a different route: it builds an adversarial attack against the classifier and lets the diffusion model’s own denoising process project this attack back onto the manifold of realistic images, turning an imperceptible perturbation into a semantically meaningful one.
DVCE ( Augustin et al., 2022 ) starts the reverse diffusion from a partially noised version of the input, rather than pure noise, and steers the process by projecting the gradient of an adversarially robust classifier onto a cone around the target classifier’s own gradient direction whenever the two disagree, avoiding non-semantic changes.
More recently, MaskDiME ( Guo et al., 2026 ) improves on DiME’s efficiency and spatial precision with a training-free, adaptive dual-mask mechanism guided by classifier gradients that restricts updates to a localized region rather than the whole image.
Regardless of the specific guidance scheme, diffusion-guidance methods must reapply their guidance at every one of many denoising steps, making inference slow: DiME’s inner diffusion loop scales quadratically with the number of diffusion steps, and even FastDiME’s one-step approximation, despite yielding a roughly 20 × \times empirical speedup, only reduces this to a linear scaling and remains markedly slower than a single forward pass. ACE and DVCE compound this same per-step cost further, respectively adding an adversarial attack and a robust-classifier gradient computation at every step. • CFM. LeapFactual ( Cao et al., 2025 ) builds on Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) to generate counterfactuals. It learns a class-conditional generative flow from a Gaussian prior to the latent space of a pretrained VAE, and repurposes this flow for counterfactual generation through a lift-and-land procedure. Given an input, its VAE encoding is first lifted toward the prior under the input class by solving the learned ODE backward, and then landed back into the latent space under the target class by solving the ODE forward. This “leap” must be repeated a dataset-dependent number of times, with each leap requiring a VAE decoding and a classifier query. Our work also builds on CFM, but uses it in a fundamentally different way. We directly learn a transport from an input image to its counterfactual. This avoids (i) the need for multiple costly leaps, (ii) the intermediate traversal through a prior space, and (iii) VAE encoding and decoding, whose reconstruction fidelity can limit the quality of the generated counterfactuals.

blocks.en: Our contributions. To address the drawbacks of the previous methods, our contributions are as follows:
blocks.zh: 我们的贡献。 为解决以往方法的缺陷,我们的贡献如下:

blocks.en:
• We introduce CounterFlow, the first CFM framework that directly conditions the vector field on both the source and target class, enabling a single model to transport examples between any pair of classes in their original pixel representation.
Moreover, CounterFlow generates a counterfactual by integrating a single (learned) ODE from source to target, with no additional VAE decoding or iterative optimization at inference. • To enable the learning of the transport map, we introduce two complementary contributions: a latent-space nearest-neighbor pairing strategy and an auxiliary classification loss. The pairing algorithm leverages the embedding space of a pretrained VAE to associate each source example with a semantically similar target example, thereby reducing the transport distance that the flow must learn. The auxiliary classification loss further guides the flow toward transformations that induce the desired change in the classifier’s prediction. • We provide an empirical evaluation covering conditional validity, plausibility, and computational efficiency, a combination rarely reported together in prior work, demonstrating that CounterFlow matches or improves on state-of-the-art generation quality at a fraction of the computational cost of GAN- or diffusion-based alternatives.

blocks.en: 2 Background on Counterfactual Explanations
blocks.zh: 2. 反事实解释的背景

blocks.en:

blocks.en: 5.1 Setting

blocks.en:
Datasets. We evaluate CounterFlow on two standard image classification benchmarks: MNIST and CIFAR-10 , MNIST consists of 70,000 70{,}000 grayscale images of handwritten digits belonging to 10 10 classes, with a spatial resolution of 28 × 28 28{\times}28 pixels.
CIFAR-10 contains 60,000 60{,}000 color images of size 32 × 32 32{\times}32 pixels, evenly distributed among 10 10 object categories.
These two datasets provide complementary evaluation settings, ranging from a simple handwritten digit classification task to a natural image classification benchmark.
For all experiments, we use the standard training and test splits provided with each dataset. Section A.4 discusses why we do not extend the comparison to larger benchmarks such as ImageNet.

CIFAR-10包含有60,000个60{,}000个大小32×32个32相的彩色相像素32个像素,均匀分布在10个对象类别中.
这两个数据集提供了互补的评价设置,从简单的手写数字分类任务到自然图像分类基准.
对所有实验,我们使用每个数据集所提供的标准训练和测试分数. A.4节讨论了我们为什么不将比较扩大到更大的基准,如ImageNet。

blocks.en: CounterFlow’s inference. For all quantitative evaluations, CounterFlow is integrated via the Euler solver with 40 steps. This fixed-step solver provides a more deterministic evaluation protocol and allows a fair comparison of the computational cost across methods. For qualitative visualizations, we instead use the Dormand–Prince solver ( Dormand and Prince, 1980 ) ( dopri5 ) to obtain smoother trajectories and higher-quality visual results.

blocks.en:
Methods. We compare CounterFlow 2 2 2 The hyperparameters of CounterFlow are listed in Appendix. against three recent counterfactual generation methods: C3LT ( Khorram and Fuxin, 2022 ) , FastDiME ( Weng et al., 2024 ) , and LeapFactual ( Cao et al., 2025 ) , where we use the official implementations.
Among diffusion-guidance methods, we retain only FastDiME as a representative baseline: DiME and ACE are prohibitively expensive to run at scale due to their inner-loop or per-step attack computations; DVCE requires an adversarially robust classifier, a constraint that our method does not rely on and that we therefore do not impose in our experiments; and MaskDiME’s masking mechanism restricts edits to a localized region, which conflicts with our evaluation setting where the change may need to affect the whole image.
Beyond this choice, neither of the two remaining baselines, namely LeapFactual and FastDiME, is applicable to both datasets.
LeapFactual relies on a compact VAE latent space to remain tractable, which does not scale to CIFAR-10 without dominant reconstruction artifacts and a much costlier latent flow, so we evaluate it only on MNIST.
Conversely, FastDiME depends on pretrained OpenAI diffusion models built for natural images, so we evaluate it only on CIFAR-10.

blocks.en: 6 Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en: Existing image counterfactual generation methods often require heavy generative backbones, including diffusion models or multiple class-specific generative networks, making their deployment computationally demanding. CounterFlow demonstrates that Conditional Flow Matching provides a significantly simpler alternative. By learning a single target-conditioned transport field and requiring only one ODE integration at inference, our method achieves competitive or superior counterfactual quality while substantially reducing computational complexity. We believe this constitutes an important step toward making counterfactual explanations practical for interactive decision-support systems, where explanations must be generated quickly and consistently.
blocks.zh: 现有的图像反事实生成方法往往需要重的基因骨干,包括扩散模型或多类特有基因网络,使其部署在计算上要求很高. 逆流显示,有条件的流相匹配提供了明显更简单的替代品. 通过学习一个单一的目标有条件的运输领域,并且只需要一个ODE在推论上集成,我们的方法实现了竞争或优异的反事实质量,同时大大降低了计算的复杂性. 我们认为,这是为互动决策支助系统提供反事实解释的一个重要步骤,必须迅速和一致地作出解释。

blocks.en: Despite these encouraging results, several limitations remain. First, our experiments are restricted to relatively low-resolution image datasets. Evaluating CounterFlow on larger-scale benchmarks such as ImageNet or high-resolution generative datasets would provide further evidence of its scalability. Second, our latent-space pairing strategy currently relies on nearest-neighbor retrieval using a pretrained encoder, which introduces an additional preprocessing step. Finally, while Conditional Flow Matching substantially reduces inference complexity compared to diffusion models, solving an ODE remains more expensive than a single feed-forward network.
blocks.zh: 尽管取得了这些令人鼓舞的成果,但仍存在若干限制。 首先,我们的实验仅限于相对低分辨率的图像数据集. 评价对策 采用更大的基准,如ImageNet或高分辨率基因数据集,将进一步证明它的可扩展性。 第二,我们的潜在空间配对策略目前依赖于使用事先训练的编码器进行最近的邻接检索,这引入了额外的预处理步骤. 最后,虽然与传播模型相比,有条件的流量匹配大大降低了推论的复杂性,但解决ODE仍然比单一的向导网络更为昂贵.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en: We presented CounterFlow, a Conditional Flow Matching framework for visual counterfactual explanation generation. Unlike previous approaches relying on GANs or diffusion models, CounterFlow directly learns a target-conditioned transport field between image classes in pixel space. Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art counterfactual validity while remaining competitive in image realism and substantially reducing computational requirements.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了"逆流"(CounterFlow),一个用于视觉反事实解释生成的有条件流量匹配框架. 与以往依赖GAN或扩散模型的方法不同,ConfaceFlow直接在像素空间的图像类之间学习一个目标条件化的传输场. 对MNIST和CIFAR-10的实验表明,拟议方法在图像现实主义方面保持竞争力并大幅减少计算要求的同时,实现了最新水平的反事实有效性。

blocks.en: Beyond counterfactual explanations, CounterFlow illustrates that target-conditioned flow matching can efficiently learn semantic transformations directly between complex data distributions, without relying on an intermediate noise distribution. Future work will investigate its application to larger-scale datasets and other data transformation tasks, including domain adaptation, semantic image editing, and robust model analysis.
blocks.zh: 除了反事实解释外,ConfaceFlow还表明,目标有条件的流相匹配可以在复杂的数据分布之间直接有效地学习语义转换,而无需依赖中间噪声分布. 今后的工作将调查其对更大规模数据集和其他数据转换任务的应用,包括域名调整,语义图像编辑,以及强力模型分析等.

blocks.en: This work introduces a method for generating visual counterfactual explanations of image classifiers, evaluated on the standard MNIST and CIFAR-10 benchmarks, which do not contain personal or sensitive data. As with other counterfactual-explanation and image-editing methods, the underlying generative technology could in principle be misused to produce misleading edited images of real people; we mitigate this risk by restricting our experiments to non-human-identifying benchmark datasets and by releasing the method as a tool for model interpretability rather than for unconstrained image generation.
blocks.zh: 这部作品引入了对图像分类器产生视觉反事实解释的方法,在标准MNIST和CIFAR-10基准上得到评价,这些基准不含个人或敏感数据. 与其他反事实解释和图像编辑方法一样,基础基因技术原则上可以被滥用,产生误导性编辑真实人物的图像;我们通过将我们的实验限制在非人类识别基准数据集上,并释放该方法作为模型可解释性的工具,而不是用于不受约束的图像生成,来减轻这一风险.

Explained classifier. A counterfactual method should not depend on the specific classifier it explains. Table 5 therefore keeps CounterFlow unchanged and only substitutes f f , comparing the RepVGG-A2 used throughout the paper with a deliberately mis-specified variant, namely the same network evaluated without its input normalization, which drops its accuracy to 86.3 % 86.3\% , and with an adversarially robust PreActResNet-18 ( Gowal et al., 2021 ) .
The mis-specified classifier is explained as well as the original one: validity stays at 100 % 100\% and both FID scores remain within two points of the default, indicating that CounterFlow does not require the explained model to be accurate, only that it defines an exploitable decision boundary.
The robust classifier behaves differently: validity drops to 83.5 % 83.5\% , while FID t reaches the lowest value we observe ( 55.72 55.72 ).
This is consistent with what adversarial training is designed to achieve, namely flattening the decision boundary and suppressing the small non-robust directions that a gradient-based guidance term can exploit, so that ℒ Cla \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Cla}} pushes less strongly and a fraction of the samples never crosses the boundary.
The counterfactuals that do cross must therefore carry a genuine, large-scale semantic change, which is what brings them closer to the target distribution; note that the 16.5 % 16.5\% of samples that remain in the source class can only inflate FID t , so this value is, if anything, pessimistic.
Explaining a robust model is thus harder for CounterFlow, but yields more plausible counterfactuals, which is coherent with diffusion-based methods that explicitly require an adversarially robust classifier ( Augustin et al., 2022 ) .

blocks.en: A.4 Choice of datasets
blocks.zh: A.4 数据集的选择

blocks.en:
We restrict our experiments to MNIST and CIFAR-10, the largest settings in which all compared methods can be run with their official implementations, the same classifier, and the same evaluation protocol.
For instance, extending this comparison to ImageNet raises the following issues.
blocks.zh:
我们的实验仅限于MNIST和CIFAR-10,这是所有比较方法可以随其正式执行运行的最大设置,同样的分类器,以及相同的评价协议.
例如,将这种比较扩大到ImageNet就提出了以下问题。

blocks.en:
Baselines. C3LT requires a separate model for each pair of classes, i.e. , 499,500 499{,}500 models for the 1,000 1{,}000 classes of ImageNet.
Hence, its ImageNet experiments are qualitative, restricted to five pairs of classes, and use latent codes sampled from a pretrained GAN rather than real images ( Khorram and Fuxin, 2022 ) .
LeapFactual relies on a latent space in which inputs can be faithfully encoded, and each of its leaps requires decoding the latent code and querying the classifier; its only large-scale experiment is a binary task on images generated by a pretrained GAN ( Cao et al., 2025 ) .
Diffusion-based methods do apply to ImageNet, but at a high cost: on CIFAR-10, FastDiME already requires about 900 × 900\times more FLOPs per counterfactual than CounterFlow ( Table 1(a) ), and ACE is evaluated on only three pairs of ImageNet classes ( Jeanneret et al., 2023 ) .
blocks.zh:
基线。 C3LT要求每对类都有一个单独的模型,即: 499,500 499{,}1000 1{,}000个类的ImageNet的500个模型.
因此,其ImageNet实验是定性的,仅限于五对类,并使用从经过预先训练的GAN而不是从真实图像中取样的潜伏代码(Khorram和Fuxin,2022年)。
LeapFact依赖于一个潜在的空间,其中输入可以忠实地被编码,而它的每一个跳跃都需要解码潜在代码并查询分类器;它唯一的大规模实验是在预先训练过的GAN(Cao等,2025年)生成的图像上进行二进制的任务.
基于扩散的方法确实适用于ImageNet,但成本很高:在CIFAR-10上,FastDIME已经要求每个反事实比ConfaceFlow(表1(a))多出约900×900\的FLOP时间,ACE只接受三对ImageNet类的评价(Jeanneret等,2023年).

blocks.en:
Evaluation. Our FID s and FID t are computed against the test images of a single class, whereas ImageNet provides only 50 50 validation images per class, which makes such estimates unreliable.
Moreover, the number of ordered source-target pairs grows from 90 90 to 999,000 999{,}000 .
As noted by Jeanneret et al. (2023) , counterfactual explanation methods still lack an appropriate testbed on such complex datasets.
blocks.zh:
评价。 我们的FID s和FID t是根据单个类的测试图像来计算的,而ImageNet每类只提供50个验证图像,这使得这种估计不可靠.
此外,订购源目标对的数量从90个90个增加到999 000个999{,}000个。
Jeanneret等人(2023年)指出,反事实解释方法仍然缺乏对这种复杂数据集的适当检验。

blocks.en:
CounterFlow. In principle, CounterFlow applies to ImageNet by adapting its U-Net architecture.
However, unlike the baselines, which build on generative models pretrained at a considerable computational cost, CounterFlow would have to be trained from scratch in pixel space, which exceeds our computational budget.
Moreover, the number of source–target contexts ( y 0 , y 1 ) (y_{0},y_{1}) grows quadratically with the number of classes, so that each context would be seen less often during training.
We leave this large-scale study to future work.
blocks.zh:
逆风. 原则上,CounterFlow通过调整其U-Net架构适用于ImageNet.
然而,与基于先入为主的模型的基线不同,这些模型以相当高的计算成本预先训练,Conforlow必须从头到尾地在像素空间中训练,这超出了我们的计算预算.
此外,来源-目标背景(y 0,y 1)(y_{0},y_{1})的数量与课程数量成四倍地增长,这样在培训期间,每个背景都较少被看到.
我们把这项大规模研究留给今后的工作。
